study type: Systematic Review of Retrospective Cohort and Cross-sectional Studies
cohort: The study examined antenatal and perinatal outcomes in refugee women compared to non-immigrant women in high-income countries, drawing data from various source countries including Eritrea, Somalia, Afghanistan, Iraq, and Syria.
finding: Despite access to better healthcare services in high-income countries, refugee women experienced worse antenatal and perinatal outcomes, including higher rates of miscarriages, stillbirths, and perinatal mortality, potentially due to late or lack of attendance at antenatal care.
